title: CSTB workers' protest sit-in against labor conditions and police restrictions
location: Planned at Ministry of Labour/administrative towers, then meeting at Bourse du Travail, Cotonou
scope: CSTB planned a sit-in at the Ministry of Labour; access to administrative towers was blocked by police, so protesters moved to the Labour Exchange and held a meeting that police subsequently stopped. It is unclear whether the crowd reached 50.
organizer: Confédération Syndicale des Travailleurs du Bénin (CSTB), with workers and union members.
threshold_50_evidence: Sources refer to workers and protesters but publish no headcount; the number of unions or workers in the broader labor sector is not attendance evidence.

start_date.summary: CSTB's account and contemporaneous reporting place the action on 21 Nov 2024.

end_date.summary: The meeting was interrupted on 21 Nov; no later continuation identified, but full cessation time is unstated.

location.summary: CSTB moved from the blocked Ministry of Labour administrative towers to a meeting at the Labour Exchange in Cotonou.

organizer.summary: The CSTB and workers/members organized the action.

demands.summary: The union opposed living-cost pressures, delayed/ineffective social negotiation, and police restrictions on assembly; demanded dialogue and better labor conditions.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Neither report provides a numerical or qualitative size estimate sufficient to verify 50.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence is described; keep unknown.

state_response.summary: Police blockade and loudspeaker removal/order to disperse are described; no arrests or injuries are reported.

notes: The source describes both a planned government-ministry sit-in that was physically prevented and a subsequent meeting/protest at the union Labour Exchange that occurred. This is a direct domestic state-targeted mobilization, but no attendance estimate verifies the 50-person cutoff. The coalition letter supports the complaint but is not an independent news account.
open_questions: Was the Labour Exchange meeting attended by 50 or more people simultaneously?
Did the police interruption end the meeting, and at what time?
Were there any arrests or negotiations not reported by this source?
